chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught game while he was in the state of Ihram, whether the Muhsil (one out of Ihram) could eat from it? He said, 'There is no harm; the redemption (Fida') is upon the Muhrim.'

And this permission for the Muhsil to eat what the Muhrim catches applies only if the game was caught in the Hal (open land). And if the game was caught in the Haram (sanctuary), then it is not permissible to eat it under any condition.

key_terms.اَلْحَرَمُ: The sacred sanctuary (e.g., Mecca or Medina) where hunting is restricted
key_terms.اَلْحِلُّ: The open land outside the sacred precincts of Mecca
key_terms.اَلْفِدَاءُ: Redemption or compensation (usually in the form of food or animals) for breaking Ihram rules
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One who has exited the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a non-pilgrim eat game caught by a pilgrim in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distribution of liability in hunting violations, establishing that the *Fida'* (redemption) burden rests exclusively on the one who entered the state of Ihram, thereby permitting others to consume the game. The Imam further refines this ruling by distinguishing between the general sanctuary (*Haram*) and the specific sacred precincts, prohibiting consumption entirely if the catch occurred within the inner sanctum. This distinction highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding the spatial validity of ritual restrictions during Hajj and Umrah.
